context: A linked 4x4 SPLOM of 200 iris-like points across 3 species (setosa, versicolor, virginica), with KDE density curves on the diagonal and brush-to-highlight cross-filtering across all 12 scatter cells.
first_impression: Clean and well-restrained — the 16-cell grid reads as a single conceptual unit rather than 16 independent views, and the 3-color Tol palette stays well within perceptual limits.
what_works: Colorblind-safe 3-color palette delivers strong species separation in petal dimensions; diagonal KDE ghost-plus-foreground layer design preserves full-data context during brushing without adding visual clutter.
what_doesnt: The upper-left 2x2 sepal-vs-sepal cells appear nearly blank in the screenshot — points at r=3.5 with 0.55 opacity vanish into undifferentiated overlap where species are least separable, undermining the matrix's ability to communicate what those dimensions show; the right edge of the SVG is also slightly clipped, hiding portions of the petal-width column.
